title: Shaken Iced Matcha Latte
changes_from_base: Matcha shaken with warm water and poured over iced milk instead of espresso and steamed milk.
summary: A cool, grassy iced latte in five minutes: matcha shaken hard with warm water until foamy, then poured over cold milk and ice, with an optional touch of maple.
equipment: small jar with a tight lid (or a bowl and matcha whisk)

steps.title: Sift
steps.text: Sift the matcha straight into the jar. Matcha is so fine that it clumps in storage, and the sieve stops those clumps ending up as gritty specks in the glass.

steps.title: Shake
steps.text: Add the warm water, close the lid firmly and shake hard for 20-30 seconds until the mixture is smooth and covered in fine foam. Without a jar, whisk it in a bowl with quick zigzag strokes. Stir in the maple syrup now if you want it sweet.

steps.title: Pour
steps.text: Fill the glass with ice and add the cold milk, then pour the green matcha over the top, stir and drink at once.

tips: The most common mistake is using water straight off the boil, which scorches the flavour; let the kettle rest 3-4 minutes first.
Shake longer than you think. Undissolved matcha settles as sludge at the bottom.
safety: Plant milks work well; oat and soy give the creamiest result, but check the allergen label.
storage: Make it fresh; matcha dulls and separates within an hour. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
